arena: Classic Generic procedural_v2 11x9 two-player, reply-search root256/slate8/opponent64
source: Previously inspected exact post-opponent-turn slate observations from response-state-boundary fit seed6343000 and validation seed6343100; no new maps, model training, or search runs
method: Compute the native score analytically from each side's 16 aggregate material/economy features and serialized rules after the searched opponent turn. The original frozen-head input also carried the pre-reply static score; the analytic formula does not use that stale feature or the frozen spatial encoder. Exclude any slate containing a terminal-magnitude candidate. Attribute the remaining score error to grave objects absent from the aggregate vector and income/upkeep of owned cells outside a province. Reconstruct both omissions directly from raw cells as a consistency check.
verification: 342 Python tests passed and Ruff checks passed on SSH server; deterministic two-case tests cover exact coarse score and both omitted terms
interpretation: Once the exact searched opponent successor is available, these aggregate features plus known rule constants almost reproduce the native reply-search selection without a learned value head. Grave and province-less-cell omissions explain every nonterminal score mismatch. The prior frozen-encoder two-layer head's poor post-reply selection is therefore not evidence that its aggregate input lacks most score information; its objective, optimization, terminal handling, or interaction with the stale pre-reply score need separate diagnosis. This is an offline successor-state oracle, not a deployable instant student, full-game strength result, or Elo. Predicting the opponent successor without performing the native search remains unresolved.
